plan: My value for the prize is $23. Given that values are uniformly distributed, I expect other bidders to have values around $24.5 on average. To maximize my profit, I should bid slightly below my value to ensure a positive expected payoff if I win. Bidding $22.9 balances the risk of overpaying against the chance of winning. This bid is competitive enough to win if others undervalue the item, while still ensuring a profit margin.

Given my value of $18, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize profit if I win. Assuming others bid close to their values, bidding $17.5 could win if their values are lower. If they bid higher, I lose but incur no cost. This strategy balances winning potential and profit maximization.

Given my private value of $25, I aim to bid slightly below my value to ensure profit if I win, while also considering the risk of overbidding. Assuming others bid near their value, I'll bid $22. This maximizes potential profit if I win and minimizes loss if I lose. I expect others may bid close to their values, so bidding too high risks paying more than my value. This strategy balances winning chances and profit.
